title: 3rd Stopping Place 2nd Truth In Sum The Indication Of Mercifulness To Unity And Oneness

questions.question: What two ideas does the passage say the truth of mercifulness proves?
questions.answer: It proves divine unity and also oneness shown within that unity.

questions.question: How is mercy described in relation to all things?
questions.answer: It is presented as something that reaches everything and includes all beings.

questions.question: Which living beings receive this nurturing mercy according to the passage?
questions.answer: All animate beings receive it, especially those that have just entered worldly life.

questions.question: What qualities mark the way this nurturing is carried out?
questions.answer: It is done with great order, precision, and consistency.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to the needs of living beings?
questions.answer: Their needs are delivered to them, and none of them are left out.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by saying mercy reaches all individuals at the same instant?
questions.answer: It implies a power and control that are not limited by place, number, or timing.

questions.question: How does the passage connect regular care for creatures with belief in one Creator?
questions.answer: It treats that universal and simultaneous care as evidence that one Lord manages all life.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the truth of opening and the truth of mercifulness?
questions.answer: Both are said to point clearly to unity: one through the ordered shaping of beings, and the other through the ordered care and provision given to living creatures.

questions.question: At the end of the passage, what did the traveler witness next?
questions.answer: He witnessed the Third Truth at the Third Stopping-Place.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the main role of mercifulness?
questions.answer: It cares for living beings by sustaining them and meeting their needs.

questions.question: Does the passage present mercy as limited to a few creatures or spread across creation? Explain.
questions.answer: It presents mercy as spread across all creation, reaching every animate being.

questions.question: What feature of this mercy shows that it is not random?
questions.answer: It operates in an orderly and regular way.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the treatment of beings that are new to life?
questions.answer: It says they are especially nurtured and provided for with careful attention.

questions.question: How does the passage rule out neglect in divine care?
questions.answer: It says no individual is overlooked.

questions.question: What is the significance of mercy reaching all individuals everywhere at one time?
questions.answer: It shows universal command and presence over all creatures at once.

questions.question: What larger belief does this universal mercy support?
questions.answer: It supports belief in the unity and oneness of Allah.

questions.question: How is the truth of mercifulness similar to the truth of opening?
questions.answer: Both function as signs that point to one divine source behind creation and care.

questions.question: How is the truth of mercifulness different from the truth of opening in focus?
questions.answer: Opening focuses on the ordered formation of beings, while mercifulness focuses on nourishing and sustaining living beings.

questions.question: What transition does the final sentence make?
questions.answer: It moves from the second truth to the traveler’s witnessing of the third truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the formation of all beings under the truth of opening?
questions.answer: Their forms are made and unfolded in a regular and orderly way.

questions.question: Why is that important in the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: Because such order is taken as strong evidence of divine unity.

questions.question: What is the central claim made about the truth of mercifulness?
questions.answer: Its all-encompassing care for living things also points to divine unity and oneness.

questions.question: Which category of beings is the passage mainly concerned with under mercifulness?
questions.answer: It is mainly concerned with animate beings.

questions.question: Why does the passage highlight those who have just come into life?
questions.answer: Because they clearly need immediate support, so their care strongly displays mercy.

questions.question: What is emphasized about the delivery of necessities?
questions.answer: They are provided in an organized way and without omission.

questions.question: How does simultaneity strengthen the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: If all are cared for at the same time, that suggests one unlimited Lord over all, not separate powers.

questions.question: What phrase in the passage shows that mercy is not local or partial?
questions.answer: The idea that it reaches all individuals everywhere shows that it is universal.

questions.question: What combined conclusion does the passage draw from universal mercy?
questions.answer: That there is both unity and oneness within unity in the divine rule over creation.

questions.question: What does the traveler’s next step in the passage show about the structure of the work?
questions.answer: It shows the work is organized as a journey through successive truths or stopping-places.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the truth of opening show through the ordered shaping of beings?
questions.answer: It shows divine unity in a very clear way.

questions.question: What does the truth of mercifulness do for animate beings?
questions.answer: It nourishes them and provides what they need for life.

questions.question: Which group is mentioned as receiving special notice within animate beings?
questions.answer: Those newly entering life are especially mentioned.

questions.question: What does “order and regularity” add to the meaning of mercy here?
questions.answer: It shows that mercy is wise, measured, and purposeful rather than accidental.

questions.question: If necessities reach living beings consistently, what can a reader infer?
questions.answer: A reader can infer that a deliberate provider is caring for them.

questions.question: Why is the claim that none are forgotten important?
questions.answer: It supports the idea of complete and universal care without exception.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by mercy reaching everyone at the same moment?
questions.answer: It means divine care extends to all creatures together without delay or limitation.

questions.question: What theological conclusion follows from that simultaneous reach?
questions.answer: It points to one God whose care and control embrace all beings.

questions.question: What kind of proof is being used in this passage: emotional, historical, or observational? Explain.
questions.answer: It is mainly observational, because it reasons from what can be seen in the care of living beings.

questions.question: What comes immediately after this truth in the structure of the text?
questions.answer: The traveler goes on to witness the Third Truth in the Third Stopping-Place.

questions.question: What broad reality does the passage say mercifulness covers?
questions.answer: It covers all things.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the care given to living beings entering the world?
questions.answer: It says they are supported with exceptional care, order, and proper provision.

questions.question: What does the absence of forgetfulness suggest about the one giving that provision?
questions.answer: It suggests perfect awareness and complete mercy.

questions.question: Why is “all individuals everywhere” a powerful part of the argument?
questions.answer: Because it expands the evidence from isolated cases to the whole living world.

questions.question: What is one reason the truth of mercifulness supports unity?
questions.answer: Because one coordinated pattern of care appears across all living beings.

questions.question: What is one reason it supports oneness within unity?
questions.answer: Because that same single mercy reaches each individual directly.

questions.question: How does the passage balance the universal and the particular?
questions.answer: It speaks about care for all beings as a whole and also care for each one specifically.

questions.question: What earlier truth is mentioned for comparison within the passage itself?
questions.answer: The truth of opening is mentioned as a comparison.

questions.question: What narrative function does the final line serve?
questions.answer: It signals a transition to the next truth in the traveler’s journey.

questions.question: What two truths are directly connected in this short passage?
questions.answer: The truth of opening and the truth of mercifulness.

questions.question: What does the truth of opening involve?
questions.answer: It involves the regular and orderly making and development of the forms of beings.

questions.question: What does the truth of mercifulness involve?
questions.answer: It involves caring for living beings and supplying what they need.

questions.question: What special example within living beings is mentioned to strengthen the point?
questions.answer: The example of those newly coming into life is mentioned.

questions.question: How are their needs handled according to the passage?
questions.answer: Their needs are met in an organized way, with nothing left out.

questions.question: What can we understand from the statement that none are forgotten?
questions.answer: Every creature matters and receives direct care.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the scale of this mercy?
questions.answer: Its scale is universal, since it extends to all individuals in every place.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the timing of this mercy?
questions.answer: It reaches all of them simultaneously.

questions.question: Why does universal and simultaneous mercy point to one divine source?
questions.answer: Because such complete and coordinated care fits one unlimited ruler rather than many separate powers.

questions.question: What is the main conclusion a student should take from this passage?
questions.answer: The ordered care of all living beings is a clear sign of Allah’s unity and oneness.

questions.question: After this conclusion, what does the traveler witness?
questions.answer: He witnesses the Third Truth in the Third Stopping-Place.
